problem:
Given a matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ with full rank and $m \le n$, solve the optimization problem:
\[ \mathop{\arg\max}\limits_{\substack{v \in \mathbb{R}^m \\ \| v \| = 1}} v^T A A^T v \]
using the singular value decomposition (SVD) of $A$. Determine the vector $v$ that maximizes the expression.

answer_text:
Let the singular value decomposition of \(A\) be

\[
A = U \Sigma V^T,
\]

where, since \(A\) has full rank and \(m \le n\),

- \(U \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times m}\) is orthogonal,
- \(V \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}\) is orthogonal,
- \(\Sigma \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}\) has singular values
  \[
  \sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \cdots \ge \sigma_m > 0
  \]
  on its diagonal.

Now compute

\[
AA^T = U \Sigma \Sigma^T U^T.
\]

Since \(\Sigma \Sigma^T\) is diagonal with entries \(\sigma_i^2\),

\[
AA^T = U
\begin{pmatrix}
\sigma_1^2 & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\
0 & \sigma_2^2 & \cdots & 0 \\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\
0 & 0 & \cdots & \sigma_m^2
\end{pmatrix}
U^T.
\]

Let

\[
w = U^T v.
\]

Because \(U\) is orthogonal, \(\|w\| = \|v\| = 1\). Then

\[
v^T AA^T v
= (Uw)^T U \Sigma \Sigma^T U^T (Uw)
= w^T \Sigma \Sigma^T w.
\]

Thus

\[
v^T AA^T v
= \sum_{i=1}^m \sigma_i^2 w_i^2.
\]

This is maximized under \(\|w\|=1\) by putting all the weight on the largest singular value:

\[
w = e_1
\]

or \(w = -e_1\). Therefore,

\[
v = U e_1.
\]

This is the first left singular vector of \(A\), usually denoted \(u_1\). The maximum value is \(\sigma_1^2\).

Hence,

\[
\boxed{v = u_1}
\]

up to the sign \(v = -u_1\). If the largest singular value is repeated, then any unit vector in the span of the corresponding left singular vectors also maximizes the expression.
